text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Since the rash appeared just one day ago in a 4-day-old, does the baby have any fever, poor feeding, or excessive sleepiness? Also, can you describe the rash in more detail—is it red, raised, or blistery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection (Disseminated Gonococcal Infection).

The combination of a 4-day-old age, maternal history of gonorrhea, and a pustular rash with an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles is highly specific for this condition.

REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, CSF Analysis, and Gonococcal PCR from lesions.
REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of the rash distribution.
